references.text: Jeremiah expresses God's intention to send prophets to the people, which reflects Jesus' words about sending prophets and teachers in Matthew 23:34.
God sends angels to guide and protect His people, which can be seen as a parallel to God's sending of prophets and teachers in Matthew 23:34.
Jesus speaks about the persecution of the righteous, which foreshadows the treatment of those He sends in Matthew 23:34.
Jesus warns the disciples about persecution, which aligns with the fate of those He sends in Matthew 23:34.
The parable of the vineyard owners who kill the servants sent to them parallels Jesus' words about sending and the persecution these will face in Matthew 23:34.
Jesus' lament over Jerusalem for killing the prophets directly relates to His statement about sending prophets in Matthew 23:34.
Stephen accuses the Jews of having killed the prophets, which reflects Jesus' words about the persecution those He sends will face in Matthew 23:34.
Saul's persecution of Christians in Damascus shows the type of persecution Jesus predicts in Matthew 23:34.
